{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f2001c3a124a5303e061fd1ce02800909e3d0ff841b8cb0b1ca79f051ceba587","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic signs","heading":"C — Traffic signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Traffic signs

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
The shape and color of a sign carry meaning, so a driver should still recognize a sign and respond correctly when fading light, fog, rain, snow or darkness make the letters hard to read [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
The eight-sided octagon is reserved for stop signs, which require a complete stop and giving the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffic before moving again [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
At a stop sign you stop behind any marked or unmarked crosswalk, and where there are no pavement markings or crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
An upside-down triangular sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
A pennant-shaped sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
A yellow-and-black circular sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
A pentagon-shaped sign warns of a school zone ahead or marks a school zone crossing, and a school zone covers the school grounds plus any abutting street or highway for one hundred twenty-five feet from the grounds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
The maximum speed limit in a school zone is fifteen miles per hour when children are present or when the sign specifies it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
A right-side-up triangular emblem with a reflective red border and a fluorescent orange center identifies a slow-moving vehicle or a vehicle that has made an emergency stop [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
Square and rectangular signs show traffic regulations such as speed limits and guide your speed and direction, most are white with black letters, a very important message is red with white letters, and a red outline with a diagonal bar always means no [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
A no U-turn sign means you may not turn around in the middle of a street or at an intersection [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
No right turn and no left turn signs show which direction you cannot turn at an intersection, and they are used where a one-way street is met or where turning would be unsafe [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A02
Wrong way and do not enter signs warn that traffic in that direction is prohibited, and a driver who enters a lane so marked will likely run into another vehicle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A02
A dual turn lane sign is posted over a highway lane used only for left turns from either direction, traffic from both directions shares that lane, and a turning lane must never be used to overtake and pass other vehicles [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A02
Lane direction signs are posted between divided highway lanes at the openings in the dividers where streets intersect, to remind you which side of the divider you belong on [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A02
A one way sign tells you that a cross street carries traffic in one direction only, and where one-way streets exist, consecutive blocks usually run in opposite directions [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A02
Speed limit signs show the fastest speed you may drive under optimal weather and road conditions and sometimes the minimum speed, while advisory speed signs at interstate entrance and exit ramps, black on yellow, show the maximum recommended safe speed for the ramp [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Diamond-shaped warning signs are yellow with black letters, usually appear without explanatory words, and warn of possible danger ahead with symbols or written warnings, while pedestrian and school warning signs may be yellow-green with black letters [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
A curve or sharp-turn warning means the curve ahead is too sharp to take at regular highway speed, and an advisory speed sign may be attached beneath it [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A03
A crossroads or side road warning tells you to watch for other vehicles entering or leaving the highway [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A03
A lane-ending warning shows which lane is ending, an added-lane sign advises that a lane is being added, and a merge warning means traffic may be moving into your lane, so be ready to change speed or lane to avoid a crash [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A03
A two-way traffic warning indicates that you are on, or the road ahead carries, two-way traffic [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A03
A hill warning calls for special care and slowing before starting downhill, a low clearance warning gives the height of a bridge or underpass ahead, and a slippery when wet warning calls for reduced speed on a stretch more slippery than other roads [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A03
A pedestrian crossing warning tells you to watch for and yield to people walking across the road, and a signal ahead warning tells you a traffic signal is ahead [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A04
Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped with a few rectangular, and orange is the basic color for work zone devices [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A04
Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channeling devices that alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them safely through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady-burn lights [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A04
Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to tell them that part of the road ahead is closed [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A04
The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point toward the side traffic should pass, so stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right and stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A04
Flaggers wearing orange vests, shirts or jackets use red-orange flags or stop and slow paddles to stop, slow or guide traffic safely through work zones [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A05
Not every sign appears in the handbook, most signs are self-explanatory, warning signs often use pictures instead of text, and the shape and color of a sign are strong indicators of its meaning [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A05
Guide signs tell you where you are, what road you are on and how to get where you want to go, and include service, location, route marker and distance signs [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A05
Most guide signs are white on green, motorist services signs are white on blue, and signs for parks and public recreation areas are white on brown [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A05
Guide signs placed before intersections show the direction to cities, interstate exit signs show where the exit is and its number, and advance interstate signs may add the road, location, attraction or upcoming routes and the distance from the exit [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A05
Distance signs on main highways show the distance to places and routes, other guide signs show the amenities available off interstate exits or mark designated places for travelers to rest, and some carry a symbol above a description or arrow [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A05
West Virginia and United States route markers are generally black on white, while interstate markers are red, white and blue [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]
